governance.intro: Smart YIRIBA’s governance rests on three bodies defined in its statutes: the General Assembly, the Executive Board and the Advisory Committee.
governance.source_note: The statutes of 15 May 2018 define the bodies and roles presented here. This page does not identify the current holders of the other board roles.

organs.title: General Assembly
organs.text: Composed of the association’s members, the General Assembly is the supreme and sovereign body. It provides strategic direction and oversees activities and compliance with procedures and internal regulations.
items: Meets at least once a year in an ordinary session.
Deliberates on decisions proposed by the Executive Board and adopts internal regulations.
Reviews the annual activity and financial report and approves the accounts for the completed financial year.
Elects the members of the Executive Board (Article 18).

organs.title: Executive Board
organs.text: As the executive body, the board handles Smart YIRIBA’s day-to-day management and implements its activities and programmes. Board positions are in principle voluntary.
items: Sets the action plan and budget.
Accepts donations and bequests and authorises the operations specified in the statutes outside routine management.
Sets the conditions for recruiting and remunerating programme staff.
Establishes programme directorates with operational autonomy under its responsibility.

organs.title: Advisory Committee
organs.text: On request, the Advisory Committee provides analyses, reflections and proposals for actions and activities.
items: Meets as needed.
Is convened by the Executive Board.

governance.roles_intro: Under Article 18, the General Assembly elects a six-member board. Article 14 sets out the responsibilities of the President, Secretary General and Treasurer.
roles: Represents the association in civil matters and authorises expenditure.
Handles general administration and replaces the President in their absence.
A position included in the board composition under Article 18.

principles.title: Elections
principles.text: The President is elected by vote and the General Assembly elects the board. Voters must be members of the General Assembly and up to date with their dues. Eligibility criteria are set out in Article 17.

principles.title: Extraordinary assemblies
principles.text: An extraordinary assembly may be convened at the President’s initiative or at the request of at least two thirds of the General Assembly’s members.

principles.title: Amending the statutes
principles.text: Amendments to the statutes require a General Assembly decision by a two-thirds majority of active members present. Internal regulations supplement the statutory provisions.

statutory_mission.title: Statutory purposes
statutory_mission.intro: Article 5 of the statutes sets out the association’s areas of work and objectives:
items: Entrepreneurship and project incubation
Computing and information and communication technologies (ICT)
Leadership
Open Data, free software and Open Source
Production and distribution of digital content about Mali
Girls’ science education and ICT in primary schools
Personal development and mentoring for girls
Artificial intelligence
Digitalisation of businesses and civil society associations
Training, meetings, conferences and workshops
Digital innovation: BarCamps, BlogCamps, hackathons and competitions
Awareness of copyright and its alternatives, and promotion of content that is free to use
Appropriate use of technology and awareness of social media risks
Freedom of expression and Internet neutrality
